button_link_surface_label: Example button/link truthfulness posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: Bounded next-step surface for official voter-information routes that rely on buttons, links, or CTA-style controls to move voters toward controlling pages or actions.

reviewed_controls.truth_note: The emphasized control navigates to the dedicated registration-status page; nearby copy does not imply that activation submits a lookup immediately from the current page.
The label and placement make clear that activation submits the current form rather than navigating to a different page.

control_semantics_note: Navigation destinations use link semantics and in-page actions use button semantics unless a more specific native control fits better.
visual_emphasis_note: Important destination controls may be visually emphasized, but styling does not hide whether the control navigates or acts on the current page.
label_truth_note: Control labels distinguish navigation, submit, reveal, download, and contact actions clearly enough that the next step is not surprising.
primary_secondary_action_note: Grouped controls preserve which path is the primary governing step and which controls are optional secondary help or utility actions.
same_page_vs_new_route_note: The route makes clear which controls keep the voter on the same page and which controls open a different official route.
submit_open_download_call_note: The route distinguishes submit, overlay-open, download, call, and email actions from ordinary page navigation.
keyboard_semantics_note: Native semantics remain honest enough that keyboard and assistive-technology expectations match what the control really does.
destination_title_continuity_note: Navigation control text stays close enough to the destination page title or official route label that the landing page is not a surprise.
compact_mobile_note: Compact/mobile layouts do not silently relabel or regroup controls in ways that change their apparent meaning.
